_status: ENVELOPE ONLY. UNVERIFIED. Values were read by eye from charts in a NASA slide deck; no per-launch-year values are recorded here. Do not invent any.

source.title: Variation in Predicted Orbital Lifetime Due to Launch Year
source.author: Caley Burke (NASA Launch Services Program)
source.note: The deck uses NASA's DAS-style lifetime predictions. Our model is a different one (NRLMSIS + our own decay), so this is a sanity check, not a calibration.

spacecraft.area_to_mass_source: NASA LSP median for 6U (same deck family); engine/AGENTS.md uses this value

envelopes.launch_year_span_covered: NOT RECORDED: confirm on the deck page before relying on the span

other_deck_figures: Launch year can change lifetime by up to 2.5x within 2 years and up to 5x over a solar cycle.
Example from the deck: launch in 2035 gives 1.6 y, launch in 2038 gives 7.4 y (altitude/size of that example not recorded here).
Launch slip example: 3.1 y becomes about 6.8 y with a 1.5 y slip.

test_definition.name: golden 2 (envelope version)
test_definition.rule: For each altitude, run our engine for a 6U (area-to-mass 0.007) over the SAME launch-year span the deck page shows. The minimum and maximum lifetimes we get must each be within +/-30% of the envelope min and max above. The tolerance is our own choice.
test_definition.if_span_unknown: Run the test over the whole real-Sun history 2015-2026 AND report the result as informational only, not pass/fail, and disclose that in README.
test_definition.never: Do not fit parameters to pass this test, and do not fabricate per-year points.
